title: Measurement of cerebral oxygen pressure in living mice by two-photon phosphorescence lifetime microscopy
protocol: Weigh the mouse.
Calculate the total blood plasma volume of the animal using the formula TBV [μL] = w [g] ⋅ 72 [μL/g].
Determine the required volume of Oxyphor 2P stock solution (Vss) based on its concentration and desired final probe concentration in blood.
Calculate Vss [μL] using the formula Vss [μL] = TBV [μL] ⋅ 5 μM / 250 μM.
Dilute Oxyphor 2P stock solution to a final volume of 50 μL with aqueous NaCl (0.9%).
Fill a syringe with the prepared Oxyphor 2P solution.
Anesthetize the animal with isoflurane at 4% for induction and reduce concentration to 1.5%-2% for maintenance.
Place the anesthetized mouse on a heating blanket.
Inject the Oxyphor 2P solution intravenously using a 30G needle.
Avoid having air bubbles in the syringe during injection.
Warm up the tail using warm water (about 40°C–45°C) or a heating lamp.
Dilate the tail vein by warming for ∼30–45 s.
Align the needle parallel to the dilated tail vein with the bevel facing upward.
Insert the needle into the vein in the direction of the animal body.
Inject the solution at a rate of ∼300 μL/min.
Draw a mark on the needle stem 3–3.5 mm away from the tip.
Use a large forceps to bend the needle at the mark, forming a hook.
Disinfect the hook by dipping it into aqueous ethanol (70%).
Rinse and flush the hook with Ringer solution.
Connect the hook to a 45 cm-long polythene tubing (I.D. 0.28 mm, Smiths Medical).
Connect the other side of the polythene tubing to a 10 μL syringe (Hamilton).
Fill the tubing with Ringer solution by drawing it in using the syringe.
Draw in the solution of Oxyphor 2P for cisterna magna injection slightly in excess of the desired amount, e.g., 10.5–11 μL instead of 10 μL.
Anaesthetize the animal with isoflurane (4% in an oxygen/air mixture for induction).
Place the mouse on a heating blanket and reduce the isoflurane concentration to 1.5%–2%.
Shave the neck region of the animal.
Place the animal on its abdomen on a support stage.
Bend the animal's head downward over the edge of the box.
Secure the mouse’s nose into the isoflurane tube to keep the head in the down position.
Carefully fix the mouse body with surgical tape on the support stage.
Define the injection site.
Disinfect the skin at the injection site (Kodan®).
Inject 10 μL of the probe solution at a constant rate of approximately 5 μL/min.
Insert the needle into the gap between the occiput and atlas vertebra without applying excessive force.
Direct the needle tip along the midline from the back of the head toward the neck, holding the stem of the hook parallel to the surface of the occiput until it meets the end of the occiput bone.
Position the needle stem close to the surface of the occiput after insertion.
Avoid any rotations or other movements of the needle during and after insertion.
Hold the needle with a forceps for stable positioning during injection.
Keep the needle inserted for a few seconds before removing it after completing the injection.
Let the animal wake up and wait at least 45 min before imaging.
Anaesthetize the animal with isoflurane (4% in an oxygen/air (30%/70%) mixture for induction).
Place the animal on a heating blanket and reduce the concentration of isoflurane to 1.5%–2%.
Clean the cranial window of any deposits using a microbrush, aqueous ethanol (70%), and water.
Position the animal under the microscope and fix it by its head post, leaving it on the heating blanket.
Maintain anesthesia at a reduced level (1.5%–2% isoflurane).
Keep in mind that anesthesia can affect brain oxygen levels; compare experiments using the same anesthesia.
Position the animal under the microscope for awake imaging.
Carefully affix the animal's head without inducing stress to the animal.
Use a microbrush, aqueous ethanol (70%), and water to clean the cranial window of any deposits.
Anesthetize the animal with isoflurane (4% in an oxygen/air mixture).
Fix the head post securely to prevent movement during imaging.
Include a motion detector if necessary to reject data obtained during motion.
Define a pattern of points in a selected plane for imaging.
Step through these defined points with the laser beam to generate the oxygen image.
Irradiate the sample at each point for a fixed time (excitation gate) using the laser beam.
Turn off the laser beam after the excitation gate and allow for the collection of phosphorescence during a longer interval (phosphorescence collection period).
Repeat the excitation/collection pattern for a selected number of cycles to increase signal-to-noise ratio (SNR).
Use an excitation wavelength of 960 nm.
Detect emission in the range of 740 nm < λ < 900 nm.
Adjust the number of cycles (M) to reach the desired SNR.
Adjust excitation power so that signal intensity does not exceed detector manufacturer limits.
Ensure photon counting detection using photomultipliers (PMTs) operates within the PMT linear range of up to ∼106–107 counts/s.
Avoid exceeding the upper limit of non-photon counting systems, as this can lead to signal distortion and systematic errors in phosphorescence lifetime determination.
Implement controls to avoid detector saturation during imaging to prevent errors in pO2 quantification.
Select a measurement location within a blood vessel at a selected depth.
Set measurement parameters as specified.
Record a phosphorescence decay using an arbitrary number of cycles M and maximal acceptable excitation power Pmax.
Adjust the detector gain to maximize the signal while ensuring linearity.
Adjust M so that the SNR in the data is sufficiently high (e.g., SNR>60 for photon-counting detection).
Decrease the excitation power P stepwise within the range 0<P<Pmax, keeping all other imaging parameters unchanged.
Record phosphorescence traces at each excitation power level.
Plot areas A as a function of the excitation power in log/log coordinates.
Choose the power region where the slope of the plot is approximately 2.00 (between 1.95 and 2.05).
Measure beam power with an optical power meter inserted immediately before the microscope if power adjustments are made prior to entering the microscope system.
Perform power measurements after the microscope objective if power control is performed inside the microscope.
Ensure the gating device is in the fully open position during power measurements.
Set the excitation and emission wavelengths.
Image the brain using the regular scanning mode of the microscope.
Visualize the vasculature using phosphorescence from Oxyphor 2P.
Inject FITC-dextran intravenously (50 μL, 70 kDa, 10% in 0.9% NaCl) if additional contrast is needed.
Define the locations for pO2 measurements using the vascular image as a reference.
Save the image of the vasculature for subsequent imaging sessions.
Obtain images of the vasculature directly before and after oxygen measurements.
Select settings for single point pO2 measurements.
Select several points within a vessel and/or in the interstitial space.
Perform a test run to estimate signal strength and SNR.
Adjust the laser power within the acceptable range.
Ensure the signal is within the linear range of the detector.
Record the decay signals.
Select excitation power carefully for measurements encompassing both vascular and extravascular compartments to ensure comparable signal levels in these compartments.
